payload.text: ST0031/04's close-out and dc's five run drivers are held under hv's ruling of 10 Nov, first-hand in dc's own window: "Hold until C5B9WJ is green, don't ship it unrun." RE-POINTED on vc's word the same day, because as first written this condition could never be met: it named C5B9WJ, which was never granted and has since been DENIED naming NTVCDH as its supersession, its pin bf6e5f08 having gone stale by eight commits, three of them touching source. FIRST HALF IS NOW MET. The arms ran GREEN in slot NTVCDH at head 5d7bfe37: plan_test 240 passed, 0 failed, exit 0; arngz.bats TAP plan 1..158 with 158 ok, 0 not ok, 0 skip, 0 todo, exit 0. Every count derived from the run and compared with nothing written down. vc counted the bytes rather than taking the holder's counts, and dc checked the other half of the pin: 5d7bfe37 is an ancestor of HEAD and nothing outside intent/ has moved since, so the green still describes the source as it stands. This is the first execution of any of ST0032. RELEASED WHEN hv HAS NAMED THE CUT'S HEAD, which hv has not done; 5d7bfe37 is the arms' head and not necessarily the cut's, which is why the drivers stay void and unpinned and why re-pinning now would do the work twice. One thing not to misread off this hold, recorded on intent/wip.md rather than carried here: a green on the arms is not a green on arngz.lua's engine, which the arms cannot reach at all, exec_create_space above all, and that unrun engine is the code hv's ruling was prompted by. Whether hv's "don't ship it unrun" is answered by a green that cannot reach it is hv's to say, and dc has put the question to hv.
